messages.author: 5893d17d64b5b0c2
messages.subject: Re: Packrat and Source Control
parts:
You'll also want to add .Rprofile, .Renviron, and the files under packrat.sources. Those are the files that redirect you to the private library (and support its population) when R starts up; without them, you won't use the private library by default when you pick up your project on another machine.

There's a little more detail in the Collaboration section of our walkthrough: http://rstudio.github.io/packrat/walkthrough.html

messages.author: 5893d17d64b5b0c2
messages.subject: Re: Packrat and Source Control
parts:
There is a workflow possible where you just checkin the lockfile, but it makes some presumptions.

In particular:

1. Every developer would have to install packrat manually before working with the project. 

2. No packages could be used other than those currently available on CRAN and Github.

If you want to try it, you could checkin just the lockfile, and then when you pull the change on another machine you'd need to:

1. Install packrat

2. Run packrat::packify(dir) to add the .Renviron and .Rprofile files

3. Restart R in the directory

4. Run packrat::restore() to populate the library

Jonathan.

messages.author: ab0d2be2ea8dabe8
messages.subject: Re: Packrat and Source Control
parts:
Hi Alex,

Sorry -- the collaboration section needs to be updated. But, in short, at minimum you need to upload the `packrat/packrat.lock` file, but it's recommended that you also upload the project `.Rprofile`, `packrat/packrat.opts` and `packrat/init.R`. You may want to upload the package sources as well (to ensure that dependencies are available in case you, for example, did not have internet access) but that is more personal preference.

As long as the `packrat.lock` file is available, you should be able to call `packrat::restore()` to restore the project library (and this is what collaborators should do -- clone the project, `packrat::restore()`, and then go ahead and work.)
